evidence_text: Attack description: Attackers send login requests with known usernames and observe response time differences or error message variations to determine which accounts exist in the system Potential impact: Allowed attackers to enumerate valid usernames through different API response times and error messages, affecting 30+ million GitLab users across self-hosted and cloud instances

Attack description: Attackers used account enumeration via different error messages and timing discrepancies to identify valid email addresses, then launched targeted credential stuffing and social engineering attacks Potential impact: 133 customer accounts compromised, used for targeted phishing campaigns affecting downstream users

Attack description: Automated credential stuffing using previously leaked username/password combinations with no rate limiting or lockout mechanism Potential impact: 925,000 accounts compromised through automated password guessing; attackers accessed stored passwords in password manager vaults

Attack description: Attacker crafts malicious URL with redirect parameter pointing to phishing site; user authenticates on legitimate site then gets redirected to attacker-controlled domain Potential impact: Credential theft affecting Azure AD tenants, phishing campaigns leveraging trusted Microsoft domains

Attack description: API keys hardcoded in source code, committed to version control, or exposed in client-side code/logs Potential impact: Customer secrets exposed affecting thousands of organizations, required mass rotation of all stored secrets

Attack description: Attackers reused and replayed valid session identifiers combined with social engineering to hijack authenticated sessions when session rotation and device-binding controls were insufficient. Potential impact: 134 organizations impacted, thousands of user accounts exposed to takeover risk

Attack description: Attackers exfiltrated encrypted password vaults and leveraged weaknesses in users' master password choices and key derivation parameters to perform large-scale offline cracking attempts. Potential impact: 2022–2023 LastPass incidents exposed encrypted vaults of over 30M users; attackers could attempt offline guessing against weakly derived keys

Attack description: Attackers exfiltrated encrypted vault data and attempted large-scale offline password cracking against weakly-derived master passwords Potential impact: Over 30 million users impacted; attackers obtained encrypted password vaults and could attempt offline cracking of master passwords

Attack description: Attackers exploit improper path validation to traverse directories and access configuration files, SSL certificates, or execute arbitrary code Potential impact: 150,000+ vulnerable devices exposed, arbitrary file read/write, full system compromise, used by nation-state actors

Attack description: Attacker hosts malicious website that makes cross-origin requests to victim's authenticated session on the vulnerable API, extracting sensitive data or performing actions Potential impact: Allowed attackers to steal cryptocurrency from authenticated users via cross-origin requests, estimated $2.3M at risk across 15,000+ active wallets

Attack description: Attacker adds admin:true or role:ADMIN to JSON request body during user registration or profile update Potential impact: Attackers could escalate privileges to admin by manipulating JSON payloads, affecting 40M+ developers

Attack description: The vulnerability stemmed from unsafe concatenation of user input into PowerShell commands, allowing attackers to inject malicious PowerShell code through command separators and script blocks. Potential impact: The attack leveraged PowerShell's powerful scripting capabilities to bypass antivirus, establish persistence, and exfiltrate credentials. Over 200 organizations were affected with average ransom demands of $500,000.

Attack description: Birthday attack exploiting 64-bit block size of DES/3DES allows plaintext recovery when same key encrypts large amounts of data; brute force attacks against 56-bit DES keys achievable in hours with modern hardware Potential impact: Affected 600+ million websites using 3DES; enabled plaintext recovery after capturing ~32GB of ciphertext; NIST deprecated DES/3DES for new applications by 2023

Attack description: Attacker observes multiple generated tokens, reverse-engineers math/rand seed based on timestamp, predicts future tokens to hijack sessions Potential impact: Predictable session tokens affecting millions of requests, potential session hijacking across CDN network

Attack description: Attacker accessed API endpoint exposing unencrypted customer database with no encryption at rest protection Potential impact: 9.8 million customer records exposed including passport numbers, driver's licenses, and personal data stored unencrypted

Attack description: Attacker intercepts plaintext HTTP traffic between client and server to steal credentials, session tokens, and sensitive data Potential impact: 15 million credit scores and personal financial records exposed via man-in-the-middle attacks on unencrypted HTTP endpoints

Attack description: Man-in-the-middle attack intercepting communications when certificate validation is disabled, allowing credential theft and session hijacking Potential impact: Complete compromise of internal systems, source code theft, access to vulnerability reports affecting 57 million users

Attack description: Attackers with access to configuration files could crack MD5 hashed credentials using rainbow tables or GPU-accelerated brute force in minutes Potential impact: MD5 hashed passwords in configuration files contributed to lateral movement affecting 18,000+ organizations including US government agencies

Attack description: Attacker exploited predictable password reset tokens that were generated with insufficient randomness, allowing enumeration and takeover of customer accounts Potential impact: Over 50,000 customers impacted, card data and partial personal data exposed, estimated losses and response costs in the tens of millions of dollars

Attack description: Attacker crafts malicious XML document with external entity references that the vulnerable parser processes, leading to SSRF, file disclosure, or RCE Potential impact: Remote code execution and arbitrary file read affecting 40,000+ enterprise deployments, CVSS 9.8

Attack description: Supply chain compromise via social engineering and malicious commits to trusted open source project over 2+ years, injecting backdoor through build system obfuscation Potential impact: Near-universal Linux compromise affecting major distributions including Fedora, Debian, Ubuntu; backdoor allowed SSH authentication bypass; discovered before widespread deployment
Attack description: Automated credential stuffing attack against login endpoint with no rate limiting Potential impact: 760,000 user records exposed, service shutdown

Attack description: Attacker repeatedly triggered MFA requests until employee approved one out of fatigue, then used social engineering to complete access Potential impact: Attacker bypassed MFA by spamming push notifications, leading to full network compromise and exposure of 57 million user records

Attack description: Attacker exploited business logic flaws in multi-factor authentication and account recovery flows to bypass security controls Potential impact: 27 crypto customers compromised, $15M+ in cryptocurrency stolen due to MFA bypass via business logic flaw

Attack description: Attacker sends password reset request with multiple email addresses in array format, system sends reset token to all addresses including attacker-controlled email Potential impact: Critical severity (CVSS 10.0), allowed attackers to reset any user's password by manipulating email parameter arrays, affecting self-managed and GitLab.com instances

Attack description: Attacker bypassed internal trust boundaries by directly accessing internal API endpoints that assumed requests were pre-authenticated from trusted frontend Potential impact: 9.8 million customer records exposed, $140M in damages, including passports and driver licenses

Attack description: Attackers exploited trust boundary violation between customer support portal and core authentication system, allowing lateral movement from low-privilege support context to high-privilege customer environments Potential impact: 134 organizations compromised, customer support tickets containing session tokens exposed, multi-billion dollar reputation damage

Attack description: Production access settings unintentionally made sensitive application data public Potential impact: Contact-tracing, vaccination, employment, and contact information became publicly accessible

Attack description: Attacker sets a forged identity header (e.g., X-User-Id) and calls privileged endpoints that trust it without verifying a session or token. Potential impact: 120000 user profiles and 8400 support tickets exposed

Attack description: Attacker supplies a URL that resolves to localhost, private IP ranges, or a cloud metadata host; the backend fetches it and returns the response to the attacker. Potential impact: Approx. 12,000 customer records and temporary cloud keys exposed via internal service access

Attack description: A buyer submits another buyer's order ID and cancels it before fulfillment. Potential impact: The route performs a state-changing operation on any existing order and never binds ownership or cancellable state.

Attack description: A ticket UUID leaks through an email, referrer, or screenshot and another logged-in user requests it. Potential impact: An unguessable identifier reduces discovery but does not authorize disclosure of the conversation and attachments metadata.

Attack description: Attacker sends requests without authentication headers, exploiting optional Depends() that returns None instead of raising HTTPException Potential impact: Complete authentication bypass affecting admin endpoints, potential full system compromise

Attack description: Attacker accesses debug console endpoint and executes arbitrary Python code using the PIN bypass or leaked secret key Potential impact: Over 2.3 million user records including names, emails, and encrypted passwords were exposed

Attack description: A request reaches a page, route handler, or server action without the expected middleware decision Potential impact: A routing-layer bypass can expose tenant data or mutations when handlers and data access perform no authorization

Attack description: Attacker-controlled Flight or Server Action payload data reached vulnerable reply deserialization Potential impact: A crafted RSC request could compromise the Next.js server process

Attack description: Unsafe deserialization of untrusted data in file transfer service allowed remote code execution without authentication Potential impact: 130+ organizations compromised including Hatch Bank, Hitachi Energy, Procter & Gamble; Clop ransomware group extorted victims for millions

Attack description: Malicious actor modified Codecov's Bash Uploader script to exfiltrate environment variables containing secrets from CI/CD pipelines Potential impact: 29,000+ customers affected including Twilio, HashiCorp, MongoDB; credentials exfiltrated from CI/CD environments

Attack description: Attacker modified Codecov's bash uploader script via compromised Docker image, injecting code to exfiltrate environment variables and secrets from CI/CD pipelines Potential impact: 29,000+ customers exposed including Twitch, HashiCorp, Confluent; CI/CD secrets exfiltrated for 2+ months

Attack description: Attacker sends crafted serialized payload via API endpoint, cookie, session data, or message queue that executes arbitrary code when deserialized Potential impact: Remote code execution allowing complete server takeover, data exfiltration, and lateral movement across infrastructure

Attack description: Attacker injects newlines, ANSI escape codes, or specially crafted strings into log entries via user-controlled input fields, enabling log forgery, log parsing exploits, or SIEM rule bypass Potential impact: Log injection vulnerabilities enable attackers to forge log entries, hide malicious activity, trigger SIEM false positives, and in some cases achieve RCE through log processing systems. The 2023 SolarWinds Serv-U attack chain used log manipulation to evade detection for 9 months.

Attack description: Internal employees or attackers with log access can harvest sensitive data including passwords, API keys, PII, and authentication tokens from application logs Potential impact: 330 million users potentially affected; passwords stored in plaintext in internal logs; $150M+ in remediation and compliance costs

Attack description: Insider threat with no audit trail of data access patterns, enabling undetected mass data exfiltration over months Potential impact: 100GB of confidential data leaked affecting 75,735 employees; $3.3B potential GDPR fine

Attack description: Attackers exploit default class loader access through data binding to achieve remote code execution via crafted HTTP requests Potential impact: Remote code execution affecting millions of Spring Boot applications worldwide, with exploitation observed in the wild within hours of disclosure

Attack description: Attackers enumerated API endpoints using verbose error messages that revealed internal paths, database schema, and stack traces Potential impact: 9.8 million customer records exposed, $140M+ in remediation costs, CEO resignation

Attack description: Attackers exploit privileged containers, unnecessary capabilities, and exposed debugging features to escape container isolation and compromise host systems Potential impact: Cryptocurrency mining on Tesla infrastructure, potential access to sensitive telemetry data, estimated $100K+ in compute costs

Attack description: Attacker hosts malicious website that makes cross-origin requests to vulnerable API endpoints. When authenticated users visit the malicious site, their credentials are used to exfiltrate data or perform unauthorized actions. Potential impact: Exposed internal APIs to cross-origin requests, allowing attackers to steal session tokens and execute privileged actions on behalf of authenticated users across 50,000+ Confluence instances

Attack description: Attacker hosts malicious website that makes authenticated requests to victim's API endpoints using victim's browser credentials Potential impact: Unauthorized data access affecting 60,000+ Confluence instances, enabling cross-origin data theft and session hijacking

Attack description: Attacker hosts malicious website that makes cross-origin requests to vulnerable API. Wildcard CORS policy allows the malicious origin to read sensitive responses, including authentication tokens and user data. Potential impact: Session hijacking vulnerability affecting 28+ million users, potential access to personal travel data, payment information, and account credentials

Attack description: Attacker crafts malicious serialized payload exploiting __wakeup() or __destruct() magic methods to achieve RCE Potential impact: Full server compromise, arbitrary code execution affecting thousands of Laravel applications

Attack description: Attacker crafts malicious serialized JavaScript object with IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expression) that executes arbitrary code during deserialization Potential impact: Remote code execution allowing complete server takeover, data exfiltration, and lateral movement across infrastructure

Attack description: Attacker submits malicious XML containing external entity declarations that reference internal files or internal network resources Potential impact: Unauthorized access to internal files, SSRF attacks, potential RCE affecting 2,000+ enterprise deployments

Attack description: XXE attacks exploit misconfigured XML parsers in containerized applications to read sensitive files, perform SSRF, or execute denial of service attacks Potential impact: Remote code execution affecting 16% of Java applications worldwide, allowing attackers to deploy web shells and gain full server control

Attack description: Attackers abuse disabled security headers, permissive hosts configuration, and exposed debug/error pages to pivot and extract secrets or hijack sessions. Potential impact: Observed in 2023 red-team assessments leaking API keys and DB credentials for SaaS apps with 100K+ monthly active users

Attack description: Attacker registers username with trailing spaces that gets truncated to match existing admin username, bypassing unique constraint Potential impact: Privilege escalation affecting 43% of web applications using MySQL with default column constraints

Attack description: Attackers craft malicious GraphQL queries to bypass authorization, access private data, or perform denial of service through nested query attacks Potential impact: Over 10,000 WordPress sites exposed to unauthorized data access; full database enumeration possible

Attack description: Attacker crafts a share link containing a base64-encoded serialized state; when the victim opens it, the app decodes and merges the object into live state, allowing prototype pollution and unsafe rendering toggles. Potential impact: Approx. 12,000 session records potentially exposed via subsequent malicious requests and 37 admin accounts affected by credential theft.

Attack description: Attacker queries API endpoint for user profile, then traverses automatically-loaded relationships to access unauthorized patient data through ORM relationship chains Potential impact: 47,000 patient medical records exposed including diagnoses and treatment histories

Attack description: Attacker exploits server-side URL fetch functionality to access AWS EC2 metadata service and retrieve IAM credentials, then pivots to S3 buckets containing sensitive data Potential impact: $80 million fine, 106 million customer records exposed, credit applications and SSNs leaked

Attack description: During CVE-2025-30066, mutable tags were redirected to malicious code that searched runner memory and wrote discovered secrets into workflow logs. Potential impact: Anyone able to read affected logs could recover credentials, and over-scoped tokens increased their value

Attack description: A crafted archive entry such as ../../app/config writes beyond the intended destination Potential impact: Archive extraction could replace application files, configuration, or startup scripts

Attack description: Attacker submits crafted HTML to a comment field; the app sanitizes with a vulnerable dependency and renders via v-html, allowing script execution in victims' browsers. Potential impact: ~120000 sessions exposed via token theft
